questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was one of the few universities in Europe where there was no language demands except for English. I also wanted to go with a friend, and this was the place where it was most certain that we would both get a spot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. There were noone to help us figure out how to log into the systems, noone to help show us the ways to the correct rooms (which were hard to find), there were noone to explain the italian university system to us and noone that tried to get us to be a part of their university culture. Very isolated experience in that sense.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance. We got one email that explained which office to get the stamp of approval that we had arrived, and that was all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find places, but it was hard to know which ones were real and what was scams. I also do know now that I paid a bit of an overprice for our accommodation, but overall I was satisfied.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there are a lot of people trying to scam you out there, so be careful. Also, it is kind of expensive compared to what the locals pay, but that is just the name of the game unfortunately.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We did not register for courses until the semester had already started. That is just how it works in the Italian universities. The courses were easy to find and a lot of information was available, but it was a bit hard to find out where and how to actually register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None as far as I remember.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Luckily I got all of the classes that I wanted. I think that is pretty normal in Milan.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it. You can change your courses until pretty late in the semester, so you can browse around a bit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was not very high. It was easy to follow the masters courses even though I am a bachelors student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had lectures exclusively. No exercise classes, no laboratory work, no group work, no student presentations, no reports and nothing to do at all except just lectures with professors talking. Not very inspiring.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ecology
Genetics, Cellular and Molecular Biology
Methods in Bioinformatics
Cellular and Molecular Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Ecology was a great course with a broad and inspiring curriculum. The professors were so nice and very accommodating of exchange students.

The rest of the courses were just okay.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of us, myself included, got our phones and personal belongings stolen/robbed. It is nice to calculate a buffer amount to be able to buy new things in emergencies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were less expensive than I expected, and also the coffee is very cheap.
Everything to do with fitness and exercise is completely out of budget and very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ESN was a great initiative to include people, but I don't think that has anything to do with the university. I do not know about any opportunities at the university itself.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know. I never saw or heard of any opportunities, so they were not very advertised for if there was any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Again, I don't know that there were any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go on day-trips to all of the surrounding cities and go on a lot of hiking trips in the beautiful italian nature. It is also possible to go to Switzerland to hike, and that is also wonderful. Furthermore you can easily take the train to Rome, Florence and Venice, and that is obviously worth the trip!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A lot of people do not speak English, so you have to wing it a bit, but other than that, the italian culture is pretty easy to understand and integrate into.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The difference in time management. Danish people are used to meeting at the exact time that was agreed upon - this is not the case in italy. People will constantly be late, and that is just part of the culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very open, kind and helpful. Everyone wanted to talk and socialize.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Expect to go there for the experience of different culture, but not for the academic level.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam period is really stressful for exchange students, as we have to go home and cannot participate in the structure they have in italy. It is very normal for them to fail exams or just to retake them if they are not satisfied with their grade, but exchange students have to go home and therefore cannot afford to fail the exams. This is not what their system is built for as it is very normal to fail.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life. It was amazing to get a friend group from all over Europe. I also really enjoyed all of the day and weekend trips.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The financial aspect was very stressful.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
